- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 30-day moving avg), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until reversion completes.
- When sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often misreads sentiment → overcorrects downward; increase forecast slightly (1–3%) to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative swings, model often averages out → forecast becomes flat; adjust for sentiment volatility by ±2–4% per swing direction.
